lines.say: Why does this crypto coin stay worth exactly one dollar?

lines.text: About $305 billion in stablecoins ride on the answer, as of September 2026.
lines.say: About three hundred five billion in stablecoins ride on the answer, as of September twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Big issuers hold cash and Treasury bills for every coin.
lines.say: Big issuers hold cash and Treasury bills for every coin.

lines.text: Under $1, traders buy and redeem for $1. Over $1, they mint and sell.
lines.say: Under a dollar, traders buy and redeem for a dollar. Over a dollar, they mint and sell.

lines.text: The issuer keeps the interest: Circle reported $668 million in Q2 2026.
lines.say: The issuer keeps the interest: Circle reported six hundred sixty-eight million in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Accountants check reserves on one date. That's an attestation, not an audit.

post.title: How a crypto coin stays worth exactly $1
post.ig:
Why does a stablecoin stay worth exactly $1?
About $305B in stablecoins existed as of September 2026 (DefiLlama).
Big issuers hold cash and T-bills; traders redeem coins under $1 and mint coins over $1, pulling the price back.
Issuers keep the interest: Circle reported $668M of reserve income in Q2 2026.
When backing is in doubt, pegs slip: USDC fell to about 87 cents in March 2023 with $3.3B stuck at SVB; algorithmic TerraUSD sank to about a penny in 2022.
Sources: DefiLlama, Circle Q2 2026 results, Axios, CoinDesk.
